source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Universal Precautions developed during the HIV/AIDS era and treated blood and specified body fluids as potentially infectious regardless of known patient status.","B":"Universal Precautions began as a food-safety program and were later transferred to hospitals to address occupational blood exposure.","C":"Universal Precautions required isolation of every hospitalized patient regardless of diagnosis, symptoms, or anticipated blood exposure.","D":"Universal Precautions replaced hand hygiene and personal protective equipment with environmental disinfection as the principal control."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC’s historical timeline describes Universal Precautions, developed in 1985–1988 in response to HIV/AIDS, as a blood/body-fluid approach applied regardless of known infection status; later concepts were incorporated into Standard Precautions.
